content: A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of all possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking itraconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you use marijuana (cannabis), discuss this with your doctor. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. This medication should not be used to treat fungal nail infections if you are pregnant or could become pregnant during treatment. Women of childbearing age should begin this medication 2 to 3 days after the start of their menstrual period to ensure they are not pregnant. Itraconazole passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Itraconazole interacts with many medications. Other drugs can affect the removal of itraconazole from your body, which may impact how itraconazole works. In case of overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests) should be performed before starting this medication and while you are taking it. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important: This information is a summary and does NOT include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: Itraconazole should not be used to treat fungal nail infections if you have a history of heart failure. Itraconazole may rarely cause or worsen heart failure. Notify your doctor immediately if you develop symptoms of heart failure, such as shortness of breath, swelling of the ankles/feet, unusual tiredness, or sudden unexplained weight gain. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially causing very serious (possibly fatal) side effects. Examples of affected drugs include certain blood thinners (e.g., ticagrelor), colchicine, medications for irregular heartbeat (e.g., disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine), eplerenone, ergot alkaloids (e.g., dihydroergotamine, ergotamine, methylergonovine), felodipine, fesoterodine, irinotecan, ivabradine, lurasidone, methadone, midazolam, nisoldipine, pimozide, ranolazine, certain statin cholesterol drugs (e.g., lovastatin, simvastatin), solifenacin, telithromycin, triazolam, among others. Uses: Itraconazole is used to treat a variety of fungal infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as azole antifungals. How to Use: Read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting itraconazole and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth with a full meal as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. Take itraconazole 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids, as antacids may decrease the absorption of this medication. If you have decreased or no stomach acid (achlorhydria) or take drugs that reduce stomach acid (e.g., H2 blockers like ranitidine, proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole), take this medication with an acidic drink (such as cola). The dosage and length of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to treatment. Take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For the best effect, take this antifungal at evenly spaced times. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) every day. Continue taking this medication until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. The capsule, tablet, and solution forms of this medication deliver different amounts of medication and may be used for different purposes. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, stomach upset, or dizziness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Itraconazole has rarely caused very serious (possibly fatal) liver disease. It can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. For any side effects, contact your doctor. In the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
